figures.name: tokenizer_tokens_per_sentence
figures.caption: Tokens produced for the same sentence in each script. Because every sentence is present in all three scripts, the columns are directly comparable: the difference is the script, not the content.

figures.name: tokenizer_information_loss
figures.caption: Share of Thaana source characters that fall inside an <unk> token, i.e. are not recoverable from the encoding at any model size. This is the measurement the romanize-first design rests on.

figures.name: tokenizer_worked_example
figures.caption: One sentence, tokenized by t5-small in each of its three scripts. The Thaana row is not a short encoding, it is an empty one: both content tokens are <unk>.

figures.name: pieces_per_word
figures.caption: How many subword pieces one word becomes. Malé Latin fragments far more than English, which is what spends the 128-token sequence budget. Counted over word tokens in running text; evaluation/tokenizer_profile.json counts word types and reports a higher mean (5.697) for the same tokenizer.

figures.name: model_size_vs_budget
figures.caption: Published checkpoint size against the 80 MB browser budget, log scale. The tokenizers that can represent Thaana belong to models one to two orders of magnitude past what a browser-only app can download.

figures.name: vocab_vs_thaana_coverage
figures.caption: The trade-off in one view: the tokenizers that keep Thaana intact are the ones carrying a quarter-million-entry vocabulary. Romanizing buys the coverage back at a 23,505-entry vocabulary.

figures.name: training_curve
figures.caption: Validation chrF++ and BLEU across the run, split by direction. The two eval populations are drawn as separate series: epochs 1-3 were scored on the full 49,948-row validation split, the resumed leg on a 2,000-row subsample.

figures.name: training_loss_lr
figures.caption: Training loss and learning rate over the logged portion of the run. The x axis starts at epoch 3.01: the earlier session's log was lost with the Colab runtime, so the region before it is missing data rather than flat data.

figures.name: scores_by_direction
figures.caption: Held-out test scores per direction. Both directions come from one set of weights and are scored on the same underlying sentence pairs, so the gap between them is a property of the directions, not of the test data.

figures.name: heldout_vs_indomain
figures.caption: The generalisation gap. The nine news domains were held out whole, so the model has never seen their subject matter; the conversational rows are a row-level holdout from a register it does train on.

figures.name: latency_distribution
figures.caption: Per-sentence generation time under Node.js with the ONNX Runtime wasm backend. This is not browser latency and is not comparable to it.

figures.name: budget_vs_actual
figures.caption: Every numeric gate in the specification against its measured value. Bars are drawn as a percentage of the gate so gates in different units share one axis.

figures.name: acceptance_criteria
figures.caption: Acceptance criteria and open gaps with their present status. `unmeasured` is shown as its own category: a criterion with no artefact behind it is not the same claim as one that was measured and failed.

figures.name: corpus_funnel
figures.caption: Why 575,892 source rows became 285,748 training pairs. Each bar is one documented drop rule from tools/build_translation_pairs.py.

figures.name: corpus_domains_splits
figures.caption: Domain sizes and the split each was assigned to. Whole domains are held out rather than random rows, so a test score measures unseen subject matter.

figures.name: roundtrip_three_figures
figures.caption: Thaana → Latin → Thaana measured three ways on two populations. Exact match is bounded below 100% by design: ten Arabic-derived letters share one romanization, so the mapping cannot be one-to-one.

figures.name: roundtrip_failure_classes
figures.caption: What the round-trip failures actually are on real news text. The largest class is source Thaana that is not spelled canonically, which the transliterator normalises rather than reproduces.
